solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I like this pub. It appears on some maps

blocks.note: taken as written
so means in this way, like this
a bar is a drinking place

explanation.surface: Someone praising their local, which is famous enough to be marked on maps.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub that appears on maps is a decoy: the definition is the whole second sentence, read as a weather chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather charts show lines joining places of equal atmospheric pressure, so such a line is found on some maps.

clue.text: Witnesses to rising sea, being at sea

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and disordered, so the preceding words are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: People who saw the tide climbing while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Signatories sign a document, and witnesses to a contract or treaty sign it too, so both are parties attesting it.

clue.text: Footwear accessories line, one stocked by chemist

indicators.note: goods stocked by a shop sit inside it, so these letters go inside the shop's name

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
an ace is a one in cards
Boots is a big British chain of chemist's shops

explanation.surface: A chemist's shop that sells a line of shoe accessories.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is the UK high-street pharmacy chain; L and ACE go inside it to make BOOT-LACE-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Laces thread through the eyelets of boots and shoes, so they are accessories for footwear.

indicators.note: in a down entry a lift raises things, so the word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: an animal's hide is its fur
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Someone hiding in a lift from a red-haired American.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus is Latin for red-haired, the nickname of King William II, so it serves as a name for a redhead.

clue.text: Old man's weakness — old variety of pinball

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
a chink in the armour is a weak point
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Dad's guilty pleasure is an old-fashioned pinball machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pachinko is the Japanese arcade game descended from pinball, with many small balls falling through pins.

blocks.note: surface reading: the shrugging phrase of acceptance, nothing can be done
setter's reading: the word 'It' is, grammatically, a particular kind of word standing for a noun

explanation.walkthrough: The resigned catchphrase hides a grammar lesson: the first word of the clue is described by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes 'it', with I, you, she and they, as a pronoun that stands for a person or thing.

blocks.note: first meaning: measure is an archaic word for a dance, and this is a traditional one
second meaning, cryptic: the dance is made with wooden-soled shoes beating the rhythm

explanation.walkthrough: Measure reads as a unit of length and wood as a ruler; the measure is a dance and the wood is in the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional folk step performed in wooden-soled shoes that beat out the rhythm; measure is an archaic word for a dance.

clue.text: One given task, mostly divine stuff!

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a chore is a task

explanation.surface: Someone handed a job exclaims that it is mostly heavenly stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid that runs in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

blocks.note: K is a symbol for a constant in science
to be in something is to be part of it

explanation.surface: Someone who is always there as a member of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin means relatives, one's family collectively.

clue.text: Waster wanting something worthwhile on the house

blocks.note: a good is something of value
on the house means free, for nothing

explanation.surface: A wastrel looking for something valuable free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is a lazy, worthless person who idles away time and money.

blocks.note: to give someone a buzz is to phone, call them
1st, with the digit read as the letter I
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Buzz Aldrin, the astronaut, first on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz evokes Buzz Aldrin and the moon landing, but here it is a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large Galilean moons of Jupiter.

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving just the outside letters

blocks.note: dire means awful
only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A musician devastated after a dreadful performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a noun after awful; it is a verb, as in show the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to show them the way; the question mark flags the less obvious sense.

indicators.note: announcing something says it out loud, so what counts is how the word is spoken

blocks.note: to counter is to combat or oppose
a fit is an attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: A pirate in a battle declaring an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending of the answer is said like 'fit' though spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirate as an adjective or verb means illegally copied or to fake, as with pirate DVDs; counterfeit means forged.

clue.text: Drive home after accident, no doubt

blocks.note: to drive is to force
RTA is the British abbreviation for road traffic accident
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone certainly driving home after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive home' reads as a phrase but splits: the home comes after the accident.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is an adverbial phrase meaning definitely, without any doubt.

blocks.note: to reap is to harvest
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: Someone comes back to gather in the fruit crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come back into view, so the verb returns fits.

blocks.note: first meaning: a piece of ammunition fired from a gun
second meaning: a gulp of spirits

explanation.walkthrough: Shot looks like it continues the gun theme, but here it means a measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a lump of metal fired from a gun and a swig of liquor.

clue.text: His new right to keep name gets man over the line

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters of the preceding word take a fresh order
keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the fodder rearranged
N is the abbreviation for name
a right is a power or authority to act

explanation.surface: A man crossing the finish line thanks to a new right to keep his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the line' suggests a finish line; the line here is a shipping company, and the man is in charge of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipping line is a company running vessels, and the person over it, owning them, is a shipowner.

clue.text: Part of back is supporting neck

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of back, all of is and the start of supporting

explanation.surface: A physio explaining that some of the back holds up the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: Neck looks anatomical alongside back, but it is slang for snogging.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is informal for kissing and cuddling amorously.

blocks.note: first meaning: understand, recognise
second meaning: value highly
third meaning: rise in value

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at how much a reward has gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one verb are strung together to read like a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean grasp a point, value something dearly, or grow in worth like property.

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: as means like
peel is the skin of fruit

explanation.surface: A puzzle about skin that has been turned inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like one phrase; split it, and out alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out cold or out for the count is unconscious, as is a sleeper.

indicators.note: something blocking a doorway stands inside it, so one letter goes within the word

blocks.note: an exit is a door out
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A question whether gardening tools are in the way of the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Are looks like an auxiliary starting a question, but it is the verb to be in its plural form.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be, and are is a plural form of be, as in 'they are'.

clue.text: Stood our ground? Is that great?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone who held their position in an argument wondering if that was impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the stock phrase 'the great outdoors'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed phrase 'the great outdoors' means open country and nature, so this is the thing that is great.

blocks.note: surface reading: a grammar note about words with an s on the end
setter's reading: words as in having words, a quarrel, and the answer is itself a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: To have words with someone is to argue; the clue asks for a plural synonym of that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are minor quarrels, the same as having words with someone.

clue.text: Serious crime providing a dodgy dealer's proceeds

blocks.note: capital is money, the proceeds one has to invest
a fence deals in stolen goods, and a fence's means of a fence

explanation.surface: A grave crime yielding a crooked trader's profits.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods; the possessive is turned round as 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital offence is a crime punishable by death, the most serious kind.

clue.text: Fear the sound of a blade

indicators.note: asking for the sound means what matters is how a word is spoken

blocks.note: the blade of a rowing oar, and the oar itself; in British speech the r is silent

explanation.surface: Dreading the swish of a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Blade suggests a knife; it is the flat end of an oar. The homophone needs a British, non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential dread, a mix of wonder and fear.

clue.text: Fly is not flying around dump

indicators.note: letters flying around are scattered and land in a new order

blocks.note: to jet is to fly
the two words rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect that refuses to fly hangs around a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly and dump look like nouns, an insect and a tip; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, to dump something unwanted.

indicators.note: to cross something one goes over it, so one word straddles another letter

blocks.note: to spite is to hurt or annoy deliberately
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A young Girl Guide injured while getting over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brownie is a junior Girl Guide, but also a household goblin of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie in folklore is a small helpful elf, a kind of sprite or fairy.
